title: Judge the whole screen as it changes
statement: Check each screen as a whole at each moment, and withdraw used scaffolding once the learner succeeds, because correct parts can add up to clutter or two asks at once.
example: After one correct answer, a guided-practice screen showed nine stacked blocks with the proof line printed three times.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build's BrainLift records two defects on one guided-practice screen: a correct tap left nine stacked blocks with the proof line printed three times, and, after that fix was merged, a spoken stretch question and a say-back card asked different things at the same moment. Neither was a bug in any component; both were the sum of correct components, and the build's rules call the second defect simultaneity, not existence, so the stretch was kept but split off and printed quieter. Ruled-out options, hints and duplicate success boxes now withdraw on success, and a declutter gate holds the screen at 630 assertions.
